product.summary: A volunteer rota app for a food-bank charity: volunteers see and take shifts and deliveries; coordinators post shifts and match deliveries to drivers.

source.quote: We want a small app where volunteers can see open shifts, sign up for them and see the deliveries they have accepted.

evidence.value: Coordination runs on a spreadsheet, WhatsApp and phone calls today

source.quote: Today we coordinate them with a shared spreadsheet, a WhatsApp group and a lot of phone calls
Nothing has been built yet; this note is the start.
Nothing has been built yet; this note is the start.

external_systems.name: Google Workspace
external_systems.role: coordinator identity provider; already used for email and documents

source.quote: must sign them in with their Google Workspace accounts, not new passwords

peaks.what: December is the busiest month; size of the peak never measured

source.quote: December is our busiest month, but nobody has measured by how much.

availability.value: A day's outage is tolerable: coordinators fall back to phone and spreadsheet

source.quote: If the app is down for a day, Maureen goes back to the phone and the spreadsheet; that is annoying, but nobody goes hungry.

data_loss_tolerance.value: Losing the day's record of who accepted which delivery is not acceptable

source.quote: Losing the record of who accepted which delivery on the day would be worse, because parcels could go undelivered.

data_categories.value: volunteers' names, phone numbers and availability

source.quote: The app would hold volunteers' names, phone numbers and availability

data_categories.value: clients' names, home addresses and delivery notes, which can mention health or disability

source.quote: clients' names, addresses and delivery notes such as "leave with the neighbour" or "use the side door, client is in a wheelchair"

data_categories.value: clients are mostly older and housebound people

source.quote: mostly older and housebound clients

source.why: Home addresses of vulnerable housebound people together with free-text notes that can reveal disability or health.

retention.value: client address removed from the volunteer's view once the delivery is done

source.quote: must disappear from the volunteer's view once the delivery is done

sharing.value: All volunteers can see every client address

source.quote: a client's address may only be shown to the volunteer who has accepted that delivery

jurisdictions_or_rules.value: registered with the UK Information Commissioner's Office; own data protection policy

source.quote: We are registered with the Information Commissioner's Office.

requirements.value: coordinators sign in with their Google Workspace accounts, no new passwords

source.quote: the trustees have ruled that any tool coordinators use must sign them in with their Google Workspace accounts, not new passwords
Our IT is one volunteer, Dev, a retired network engineer
He knows Linux and networks

skills.value: has not built a web app before

source.quote: he has not built a web app before

operating_capacity.value: about five hours a week from Dev

source.quote: who gives us about five hours a week

constraints.text: A client's address is shown only to the volunteer who accepted that delivery, and disappears once it is done (data protection policy)

source.quote: Our data protection policy says a client's address may only be shown to the volunteer who has accepted that delivery, and must disappear from the volunteer's view once the delivery is done.

constraints.text: Coordinators sign in with their Google Workspace accounts (trustees' ruling)

source.quote: the trustees have ruled that any tool coordinators use must sign them in with their Google Workspace accounts, not new passwords

goals.note: In volunteers' hands before the November winter appeal, if possible

source.quote: Above all, something in volunteers' hands before the winter appeal starts in November, if we can manage it.
After that, it should cost as little as possible to run.
And Dev should not have to babysit it.

unknowns.question: How much will usage grow?
unknowns.why_it_matters: Counting today's users and deliveries matters first; no forecast is given.

unknowns.question: Is there a speed target?
unknowns.why_it_matters: No speed problem is named for this small rota.

unknowns.question: How quickly must it recover?
unknowns.why_it_matters: A day on the phone and spreadsheet is explicitly tolerable.

unknowns.question: Is any attack named?
unknowns.why_it_matters: None is named; the address policy sets access controls.

unknowns.question: Is any certification or audit required?
unknowns.why_it_matters: ICO registration is already keyed as a privacy duty; no separate audit is requested.

unknowns.question: What budget, if any, will the trustees set for building it?
unknowns.why_it_matters: Whether anything can be bought or paid for decides between a free off-the-shelf tool, a hosted product and a small custom build.

unknowns.question: What monthly running cost can the charity afford, and who pays it?
unknowns.why_it_matters: A charity with no running budget needs a free tier or donated hosting; this narrows every option.

unknowns.question: How many volunteers and how many deliveries a week are there?
unknowns.why_it_matters: The number of users and deliveries decides whether a spreadsheet-backed tool is enough or a database-backed app is needed, and how big the December peak is.

assumptions.text: Volunteers themselves do not have Google Workspace accounts; only coordinators must use them.
assumptions.why: The brief's sign-in ruling names coordinators only.
